papers.title: Fatigue Characteristics of Additively Manufactured Aerospace Materials
papers.abstract: This presentation documents the fatigue properties of three additive manufactured (AM) metallic systems (Ti-6-4, GRC op-84, and Alloy 718) used by NASA in various aerospace applications. These alloys were produced using the powder bed method, with the titanium alloy using an electron beam melting (EBM) and the other two alloys using selective laser melting systems (SLM). For each material a large matrix of fatigue tests were conducted and the fatigue characteristics compared to their conventionally manufactured counterparts. Build orientations and resulting microstructures are discussed with respect to the tested mechanical properties.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究对象为航空航天用增材制造合金的疲劳性能，与生物医用植入物的设计、应力遮挡或骨整合无直接关联。
llm.why_not_core: This paper addresses fatigue of aerospace AM alloys without any biomedical context, porous implant design, stress shielding/stiffness matching, LPBF for biomedical materials, or surface roughness/osseointegration analysis.

summary_zh.motivation: 研究增材制造航空合金的疲劳性能，对比传统制造方式。
summary_zh.method: 采用电子束熔融和选择性激光熔化制备三种合金试样，进行多参数疲劳测试。
summary_zh.result: 给出了不同合金的疲劳特性及构建取向对微观结构和力学性能的影响。
summary_zh.validation: 通过大量疲劳试验数据与常规制造材料对比验证。

summary_en.motivation: To characterize the fatigue properties of three additively manufactured aerospace alloys and compare them with conventionally manufactured counterparts.
summary_en.method: Ti-6Al-4V was fabricated by electron beam melting, while GRCop-84 and Alloy 718 were produced by selective laser melting; a comprehensive fatigue test matrix was performed.
summary_en.result: Fatigue characteristics for each alloy were documented, and the influence of build orientation on microstructure and mechanical properties was discussed.
summary_en.validation: Extensive fatigue testing and comparison with conventionally manufactured materials provided experimental validation.
